label: History
value: Adrian recovered from typhoid fever in Toronto.
unit: After recovering from typhoid fever in Toronto, Adrian traveled to Seven Gulls to regain his health and explore the ancient homestead of his grandparents, boarding with Lorna Vane. During his stay, Nell Carrow introduced him to Captain Saul Garrick, whose life stories and journal inspired Adrian to write a novel. He spent the summer collaborating with Captain Saul to complete The Life-Book of Captain Saul, while forming a close bond with the local community. Over the course of the season, Adrian fell deeply in love with Lorna, but maintained silence regarding his feelings due to her marital situation, departing quietly at the end of the summer in great anguish. Following the revelation that Lorna's husband was dead and her marriage invalid, Adrian returned the following summer to court her. He proposed to Lorna in the garden of the small house of dreams, and their wedding was planned for Christmas. In addition, his co-authored book with Captain Saul was successfully published, and he made plans to purchase Lorna's old property as a summer home.

value: Agatha Sowerby lived in Sowerby's Hollow in Brierley.
unit: Agatha Sowerby lived in Sowerby's Hollow in Brierley, serving as a pillar of the local church organizations, including the Sewing Circle, Sunday-school, Church Aid Society, and Foreign Missions Auxiliary. When Obed Abernethy brought the orphan girl Nell home to Grey Shutters, Agatha was quick to disapprove and later insulted Nell's looks, prompting a furious outburst from the girl that led to Nell offering a dramatic apology. Over the years, Agatha continued to keep a close eye on community affairs, raising money for church causes, organizing events, and commenting on local developments. When her quiet husband Thomas fell ill, she cared for him tenderly until his death. Following his passing, she sold her excess household items and moved into the renovated spare room at Grey Shutters to reside with Thirza Abernethy. She later traveled to Seven Gulls with Thirza and the twins to celebrate Christmas with the newly married Hugh and Nell, bringing along a plum pudding she had baked.

label: History
value: Ambrose Kerr campaigned passionately for the Liberal (Grit) party during an exceptionally intense general election fifteen years prior.
unit: During a exceptionally intense general election fifteen years prior, Ambrose Kerr campaigned passionately for the Liberal (Grit) party and publicly swore he would refrain from shaving his face or cutting his hair until his party returned to power. Following their defeat, he steadfastly kept his vow for fifteen years, growing out a long beard and hair. He frequently spent time cod-fishing with his old friend Captain Saul, and during a New Year's Eve gathering at Captain Saul's house, he entertained the guests by singing Scotch ballads and dancing vigorously with Lorna Ainslie. Upon learning around midnight after election day that the Liberals had finally won, Ambrose proceeded immediately to Augustus Palmer's barber shop in the Glen, forced the reluctant Tory barber to open his shop, and had his hair trimmed and beard shaved before sunrise. He later visited Captain Saul while clean-shaven, enjoying the fact that Nell Harcourt initially failed to recognize him. Shortly thereafter, he became engaged to Miss Winifred Tolley, agreeing to move into her green house upon their marriage.

label: History
value: Anthony Tulk is an orphan.
unit: Anthony Tulk, an orphaned nephew taken in by Mrs. Laurence Tulk, began attending Brierley school under Nell Harcourt's instruction. From the start, he displayed open hostility and disdain toward Nell, believing female teachers to be useless. He repeatedly misbehaved, such as pouring water down a classmate's neck and placing a live mouse in Nell's desk drawer. When Nell lost her temper and gave him a harsh whipping with a wooden pointer, the punishment surprisingly earned Anthony's respect. Following the incident, he began acting politely toward Nell, offering to carry her books and speaking favorably of her, declaring that her beating was 'just as good as a man's.' When Nell eventually resigned her post, Anthony engaged in two deliberate fights with other boys to process his emotions over her departure.

label: Personality
value: Aunt Euphemia is an outmoded housemother.
unit: Aunt Euphemia is an outmoded, indulgent, and easygoing housemother who believes in letting young people manage themselves. She holds traditional views on decorum—particularly regarding the clergy—and maintains a youthful, laughing outlook on life. She is deeply forgiving, cheerful, and possesses a strong sense of personal faith.

label: History
value: Aunt Euphemia's daughter Elizabeth got married.
unit: Left alone in a large house after her daughter Elizabeth got married and left for missionary work, Aunt Euphemia agreed to move to Portmaris to keep house for Nell Harcourt, Honora, Mabel, and Cressy Lindsay at Tabby's Place. She brought along her two cats, Joseph and the Sarah-cat, and eventually adopted the stray cat Smudge into her household. She spent three winters managing Tabby's Place and caring for the college girls, staying behind during holiday breaks to look after the house and animals. Following the girls' graduation from Wexcombe, she took all three cats back to her own home. Later, despite her fear of snakes, she traveled to India to inspect her daughter's mission field.

label: History
value: Belinda went to live with Miss Rosalind at Echo Cottage.
unit: Belinda went to live with Miss Rosalind at Echo Cottage when she was thirteen, taking on domestic duties in exchange for room, board, and garments. Because Miss Rosalind referred to all her young handmaidens as 'Belinda' to avoid confusion, she became known as Belinda the Fourth. She grew deeply attached to Miss Rosalind and entertained visitors like Nell and Isolde with great cheerfulness. When Miss Rosalind married Stephen Stanhope, Belinda helped with the wedding preparations and subsequently moved to Boston with the family in the autumn. Over time, she grew into a young woman and eventually married a American bricklayer named Tom, though she returned to attend Nell's wedding and remained devoted to her old friends.

label: History
value: Captain Saul spent decades as a sea captain.
unit: Captain Saul spent decades as a sea captain, experiencing wild adventures including mutinies, shipwrecks, and pirate encounters across the world before retiring to keep the lighthouse at Seven Gulls Point. When Nell Carrow and her husband arrived in Seven Gulls, he befriended them, sharing stories, tea, and companionship at both his lighthouse and their house of dreams. He maintained a strong friendship with Lorna Vane, assisting her with loans and advising that her long-lost husband be informed of his survival options. During a visit by Adrian Treleaven, the schoolmaster's grandson, Captain Saul shared his handwritten logbook, leading Adrian to adapt his life into a published novel. On the day his author's copy arrived, Captain Saul spent a joyous evening reading it, and passed away peacefully in his armchair that night with the book on his chest.

label: History
value: Cedric Stanhope arrived from the States
unit: Cedric Stanhope arrived from the States to live with his grandmother in Brierley and attend the local school taught by Nell Harcourt. He quickly formed a deep bond of friendship with Nell, whom he loved dearly as a teacher. Though quiet and dreamy, he proved capable in schoolyard games and held his ground in a fight against St. Clair Trask over national pride. Cedric introduced Nell to his imaginative world of 'Rock People' on the beach, as well as his love for poetry. When Nell introduced Cedric to Miss Rosalind Penrose, his strong resemblance to his father Stephen Stanhope helped rekindle the past connection between Rosalind and Stephen. After his father returned and married Rosalind, Cedric moved to Boston to live with them, though he returned to Echo Cottage and Brierley during summer vacations. Over the years he grew into a tall young man, played football, and began publishing poetry in magazines. At nineteen, he returned to attend Nell's wedding before making plans to travel overseas for two years of study.

label: History
value: Cressida met Nell Harcourt in a Wexcombe cemetery.
unit: Cressida first met Nell Harcourt and Honora Hollis in a Wexcombe cemetery, quickly introducing herself by her nickname Cressy and taking an instant liking to them. Her social prominence, charm, and beauty helped introduce Nell and Honora to many college circles during their time at Wexcombe. Throughout her freshman year, she struggled to choose between her suitors Hector and Orlando, while also sharing housing with Nell, Honora, Mabel, and Aunt Euphemia at Tabby's Place. During her final year at college, she fell in love with a minister named Ezra Hale, persevered against her mother's initial disapproval, and married him the week following their college completion. The couple settled on Tanner Street in the Patterson slums, where she later gave birth to children. Prior to Nell's wedding to Hugh Carrow, Cressy sent Hugh a letter clarifying that Nell and Cyril Lisle were not engaged, encouraging him to pursue Nell again.

label: History
value: Cyril completed two years of study at Wexcombe.
unit: Cyril completed two years of study at Wexcombe before putting his degree on hold to spend two years in Europe accompanying his ill mother. He later returned to Wexcombe to finish his Junior year, where he met Nell Harcourt in the park during a rainstorm by sheltering her under his umbrella. He immediately pursued her, sending her long-stemmed roses, white orchids, and personal sonnets. Over two years at college, he corresponded with her twice weekly and escorted her to events, leading observers to assume an engagement was imminent. Before Convocation, he brought his mother and sisters to visit her circle, though his family initially harbored reservations. At the end of their term, Cyril took Nell to a small pavilion by the harbor and proposed marriage. Unexpectedly, Nell refused his proposal because she realized she did not love him. Heartbroken and bitter, Cyril accused her of ruining his life before bidding her farewell. His sister Dorothy later noted that while he suffered intensely following the rejection, he would eventually recover as he had in past romantic disappointments.

label: History
value: Flossie attended school under Mr. Pidgeon
unit: While attending school under Mr. Pidgeon, Flossie was caught cheating during a spelling test by Nell Harcourt. Later, during a gathering of young girls, she successfully walked the Pembroke garden fence on a dare and subsequently challenged Nell to walk the kitchen roof ridgepole, resulting in Nell falling and injuring her ankle. When a school concert was organized, Flossie became moody after being denied the role of fairy queen due to her heavy build, though she later attended the successful event. She earned top prize for knitted lace at a local exhibition. Upon entering the Regent's class, she prepared for the Entrance exams, barely passing with a three-point margin. She went on to attend the Academy at Regent's, lodging in the same house as Frank Stockley. After passing her courses, she chose to return to Regent's for a second year rather than teach. She helped host a send-off party for Nell and Hugh Carrow, showing unusual friendliness toward Nell. Later, she spread malicious gossip claiming Nell had stolen her prize-winning story.

As she reaches adulthood, Isolde courts and marries Gideon Duckett, moving to his farm two miles away from Grey Shutters. She subsequently gives birth to two children, including a son and later a daughter named Small Nell Lucinda.

label: History
value: Lorna grew up in Seven Gulls.
unit: Lorna grew up in Seven Gulls as the intelligent and cheerful daughter of Frank Ainslie. Her early life was shattered at age twelve when she witnessed her four-year-old brother Julian die in an accident, and at fourteen she discovered her father after he committed suicide. Funded by her grandmother West's inheritance, she excelled at Regent's Academy and became a teacher at the Glen school. To prevent Abner Vane from foreclosing on her mother's mortgaged farm, she reluctantly married Rufus Vane. Following her mother's death and Rufus's departure on a voyage, Rufus vanished, only for Captain Saul to later return a brain-injured, amnesiac man identified as Rufus, whom Lorna faithfully cared for over eleven years. She befriended Nell Carrow, though her hidden grief and intense jealousy over Nell's domestic happiness caused intermittent friction before she fully opened her heart. Summer boarder Adrian Treleaven stayed at her house, inspiring mutual romantic feelings that Lorna felt bound to hide. When Hugh Carrow arranged for the amnesiac man to undergo trephining in Montreal, the surgery restored his memory, revealing he was actually Rufus's lookalike cousin Laurence Vane, while Rufus had died of yellow fever years prior. Released from her false marriage, Lorna returned to Seven Gulls and gradually accepted her freedom, ultimately reuniting with Adrian Treleaven.

Released from her false marriage, Lorna returned to Seven Gulls and gradually accepted her freedom, ultimately reuniting with Adrian Treleaven.

label: History
value: Lucy Farrow was born.
unit: Lucy Farrow was born six minutes apart from her twin brother, Robin. Following the death of their mother, Mary Farrow, the twins were taken in by Thirza Abernethy to be raised at Grey Shutters with the help of Nell Harcourt. During her childhood, she endured numerous mischievous pranks by her brother, including being pushed into mud, sprayed with water under a pump, and locked inside a toolhouse. She began attending school alongside Robin under Nell's instruction, proving to be a quiet and submissive pupil. On one occasion, Robin forced her to skip Sunday School and go fishing with the Cotton children, though she spent the time holding her religious books and regretting the misadventure. As she grew older, she took on household duties at Grey Shutters with mature grace and caution. By the age of seventeen, she inherited Nell's former porch room and began attracting the romantic interest of Ralph Pullen.

label: History
value: Nell Harcourt was born in Harborough, Nova Scotia.
unit: Nell Harcourt was born in Harborough, Nova Scotia, to schoolteacher Edmund Harcourt and Bertha Harcourt. After being orphaned, she was sent to Grey Shutters on St. Brendan's Island by mistake when an orphan boy had been expected. Despite initial misunderstandings, she was taken in by Thirza and established a lifelong friendship with Isolde Pembroke. At Brierley school, Nell was known for her brilliant imagination, her feud with Hugh Carrow after he pulled her plait, and her academic achievements, ultimately winning the Avery scholarship. Postponing college to assist Thirza, she worked as the schoolteacher in Brierley for two years. Afterwards, Nell attended Redmond College, where she earned literary recognition by winning a short story contest with 'Evadne's Atonement' and publishing work in magazines. During her time at college, she rejected marriage proposals from Barney Pullen and the romantic Cyril. Upon completing her studies and putting geometry behind her, Nell prepared for her upcoming marriage to a physician.

label: History
value: During her childhood in Brierley, Odette attended school.
unit: During her childhood in Brierley, Odette attended school under Mr. Pidgeon and was part of a close group of friends that included Nell Harcourt, Isolde Pembroke, and Opal Pettigrew. She joined the local Story Club and wrote sensible, sensible stories, though reading them aloud made her feel foolish. After finishing her studies at Regent's Academy and passing her teacher's examinations, she accepted a position teaching at Stonebridge. She later served on the Brierley Village Improvement Society committee and briefly took over teaching at the Brierley school. Eventually, she departed for the West to teach on the prairies. After returning from the West, she married Mr. Inglis, a wealthy Englishman from Winnipeg, in a lavish ceremony laden with diamonds and lace, and went on a European honeymoon before settling into a prosperous and happy married life.

label: Quotes
value: > Floating downward does not bother me when two or three of us are occupying the flat and we are able to sit upright. During those times, it is enjoyable. However, lying flat and acting as if I were deceased—that is something I simply could not do. Fear would actually kill me.

label: Quotes
value: > Will you come up frequently, Nell? Make sure to come by yourself—I need you.

label: Quotes
value: > The cemetery appears so peculiar under the moon’s light! So spectral! Nell, the time is drawing near when I will be resting in that place. You, Isolde, and everyone else will be moving around, brimming with vitality—while I will be situated there—within the ancient cemetery—deceased!

label: Quotes
value: > Everyone is aware of it. It is known to me—it has been known to me the entire summer, even if I refused to admit it. And, oh, Nell—dying is not what I want. The thought of dying frightens me.

label: Quotes
value: > I want to live. I want to live the way other girls do. I—I desire to get married, Nell—and—and—possess tiny children. You are aware that babies were always something I loved, Nell. To nobody else except you could I admit this. That you comprehend, I know. Furthermore, poor Herb—he—he cares for me and my love belongs to him, Nell. Nothing was meant to me by the others, yet he matters—and provided I could remain alive, I would become his wife and experience such happiness. Oh, Nell, this is difficult.

label: History
value: Opal attended Brierley school as a girl.
unit: Opal attended Brierley school as a girl, where she sat in front of Hugh Carrow and frequently shared school gossip and romantic theories learned from her older sisters. She was a member of the school's Story Club under the nom-de-plume of a sentimental writer, and took part in local play-acting and concerts. Following her primary schooling, she entered the Regent's class alongside Nell Harcourt and others, going on to study at Regent's Academy in Port Marlow, where she won recognition as the most beautiful student. She subsequently secured a teaching position at Delford school. During her adolescence, she was pursued by numerous local suitors, including Nelson Atkins and Wilbur Blair, and eventually fell in love with Herb Tranter. After contracting a severe lung congestion over the winter, she developed galloping consumption, forcing her to abandon teaching. Despite maintaining an optimistic front of social outings and suitors, she privately shared her terror of dying with Nell during a conversation in her garden. She died peacefully in her sleep shortly thereafter during the summer, leaving an unfinished embroidered centerpiece for Nell.

label: History
value: Mr. Pettifer moved to Brierley
unit: After moving to Brierley from New Brunswick, Mr. Pettifer acquired a reputation for eccentricity, frugality, and unusual domestic habits. He initially feuded with neighbor Nell Harcourt over her Jersey cow repeatedly breaking into his oat field. After Nell accidentally sold his cow to a buyer, she visited his home with a pink-frosted nut cake as a peace offering, leading to a warm resolution and the beginning of a close friendship between them. Over time, Mr. Pettifer offered practical, unvarnished advice to Nell regarding her teaching plans and story writing. When a thunderstorm struck the area, lightning killed his beloved parrot Nutmeg, leaving him deeply saddened. His estranged wife Emily later arrived in Brierley after seeing a newspaper prank, resulting in their domestic reconciliation, a newly cleaned house, and his return to church attendance. He continued to take a keen interest in Nell's life and writing, ultimately being invited as one of her cherished guests to her wedding.

At the end of June, his term at Brierley came to an end, and he gave a tearful farewell address to his students before being succeeded by Miss Thorne.

label: History
value: Ezra Hale studied theology at St. Columbia
unit: Ezra Hale studied theology at St. Columbia after graduating from Wexcombe. While managing the Point Prospect Mission Church during one summer, he met Cressida Lindsay at Prospect Point, and the two quickly became fast friends. Although he initially resisted becoming a clergyman, he embraced it as his true calling and delivered moving sermons. After finishing his studies at St. Columbia, he took over a small mission church on Tanner Street in the slums. He proposed to Cressida Lindsay and married her the following June, with Nell Harcourt acting as bridesmaid. By the time of Nell's wedding to Hugh, he and Cressida had children and traveled together to attend Nell's nuptials, where he offered a lauded wedding prayer.

label: History
value: Robin and Lucy are twins.
unit: Robin and his twin sister Lucy were orphaned in East Welby and taken to live at Grey Shutters by Thirza Abernethy and Nell. From his initial arrival, he constantly caused trouble through pranks, such as putting a toad in Thirza's bed, pulling girls' hair, and locking Lucy in a building while lying about her disappearance. Over time, Nell's gentle guidance helped reform his conduct, though he regularly rebelled against strict authority figures like Agatha Sowerby. Upon starting school, his mischief diminished as he burned off energy with schoolmates like Milty Gammon, and he developed a keen interest in agriculture as he grew older.

label: History
value: Rosalind lives quietly at Echo Cottage in Welby.
unit: Living quietly at Echo Cottage in Welby, Rosalind led a solitary, romantic life filled with dreams and local echoes, assisted by her young handmaiden Belinda the Fourth. When Nell Harcourt and Isolde Pembroke stumbled upon her stone house, they quickly formed a warm friendship, and Nell became a regular visitor. Overcoming her initial hesitation, Rosalind agreed to meet Cedric Stanhope, the son of her former fiancé Stephen Stanhope, and grew deeply fond of him. After Stephen returned to the region and sent word through Nell, he visited Rosalind at Echo Cottage, resolving their past rift. The two were married late that August beneath the honeysuckle trellis in her garden before departing for Boston and the Pacific coast. They continue to reside in Boston while returning every summer to inhabit Echo Cottage.

label: History
value: Rufus Vane became smitten with Lorna Ainslie.
unit: Rufus Vane became smitten with Lorna Ainslie, but she repeatedly rejected him. To force her into marriage, he threatened her mother, Rose Ainslie, with foreclosing the mortgage on the Ainslie farm, which was held by his father Abner Vane. Desperate to keep her home, Rose pressured seventeen-year-old Lorna into marrying him. Following their wedding, they lived on the Ainslie farm through the winter. By spring, Rufus grew tired of domestic life and left for Nova Scotia, where he joined his cousin Laurence Vane aboard the ship Four Sisters bound for Havana, Cuba. While in Cuba, Rufus contracted yellow fever and died approximately thirteen years before the truth was uncovered. For twelve years, the people of Seven Gulls mistaken his surviving cousin Laurence—who had lost his memory from a severe head injury—for Rufus, until a successful brain surgery in Montreal restored Laurence's memory and revealed Rufus's true fate.

Desperate to keep her home, Rose pressured seventeen-year-old Lorna into marrying him. Following their wedding, they lived on the Ainslie farm through the winter. By spring, Rufus grew tired of domestic life and left for Nova Scotia, where he joined his cousin Laurence Vane aboard the ship Four Sisters bound for Havana, Cuba. While in Cuba, Rufus contracted yellow fever and died approximately thirteen years before the truth was uncovered. For twelve years, the people of Seven Gulls mistaken his surviving cousin Laurence—who had lost his memory from a severe head injury—for Rufus, until a successful brain surgery in Montreal restored Laurence's memory and revealed Rufus's true fate.

label: History
value: Tabitha Pratt was hired as a general servant
unit: Tabitha Pratt was hired as a general servant for a few weeks at the small house where Nell and Dr. Hugh Carrow resided. Initially suspicious of Thirza Abernethy, Tabitha made peace with her when Thirza did not interfere in the kitchen during Nell's childbirth. She developed a deep, protective devotion to Nell, caring for her through the loss of her newborn infant and staying on through the summer at Hugh's request. When her sister Matilda fractured her leg, Tabitha briefly left to care for her before returning to her duties. She welcomed the household's eventual move to the larger Varley house in the Glen due to its superior cellars, pantries, and running water.

value: Thirza Abernethy lived a quiet life.

Her routine shifted dramatically when an orphan girl, Nell Harcourt, arrived by mistake instead of the boy they had requested. Though initially intent on returning Nell, Thirza softened and decided to keep and rear the girl. Over the years, she formed a profound maternal bond with Nell, taking pride in her academic achievements and character. Following Obed's death, Thirza faced financial and emotional strain, nearly selling Grey Shutters, but Nell chose to stay and teach in Brierley to preserve the home. Later, Thirza agreed to adopt two orphaned twins, Robin and Lucy Farrow. She also invited the widowed Mrs. Agatha Sowerby to move into Grey Shutters to live with her. In later years, Thirza traveled to Seven Gulls to spend Christmas with Nell and assist her during childbearing.

label: History
value: Miss Agnes Thorne was hired by the school trustees
unit: Miss Agnes Thorne was hired by the school trustees as the first female teacher in Brierley. She introduced field days to study nature, daily physical culture routines, biweekly pupil recitations, and alternative composition exercises. To raise funds for a schoolhouse flag, she organized a Christmas concert with the students. Recognizing the potential in her advanced students, she organized an after-school preparation class for the Regent's entrance exam. Despite receiving a job offer in her home district's grade school, she chose to stay in Brierley to see her entrance class through their final year. Her educational methods included urging pupils to write simply and act as their own critics, which occasionally drew skepticism from conservative community members and trustees. Under her guidance, all members of her entrance class passed their exams. When she eventually departed Brierley at the end of her tenure, she left behind a profound legacy among her students, who held her in deep affection and respect.

label: History
value: Winifred resides in a bright emerald house.
unit: Winifred resides in a bright emerald house in Seven Gulls, where she has lived for many years. She regularly visits her neighbor Nell Carrow, bonding over shared views and identifying her as one of the few people who 'know Joseph.' Known for assisting neighbors in distress, she hand-sews garments for expected infants, such as the Proctor family's eighth child, and aids grieving mothers like Nell after the loss of her newborn. She also acts as a close friend and confidante to Lorna Vane, fiercely sympathizing with Lorna's tragic past and resenting Adrian Treleaven when he causes Lorna heartache. When Hugh Carrow proposes a medical intervention for Laurence Vane (believed to be Rufus Vane), Winifred strongly opposes it out of protective concern for Lorna. During the summer, she serves as a delegate to the W.F.M.S. conference in Portmaris alongside Mrs. Thomas Holt. Eventually, despite her long-standing complaints about men, she surprises Nell and Hugh by announcing her engagement to her long-time suitor, Ambrose Kerr.
